requirements.text: (Window) A file that belongs to a registered workspace opens as an editor tab in that workspace's tab strip, beside its terminal and Console tabs. The main area switches to that owning workspace when another view is showing, and never switches to the global editor view for a workspace-owned file. Each workspace has one selected tab, which can be a terminal, the Console or an editor tab.

(Window) Files that belong to no registered workspace are kept in a separate global editor view, and the header Editor button keeps opening that view. The global strip lists only unowned files and unsaved documents that have no workspace home, as a plain list with no grouping.

(Core rule, shown in the window) A file belongs to the workspace whose root folder contains the file's path. When more than one registered workspace's root contains the path, the deepest root wins. A file outside every workspace root belongs to no workspace.

(Window) Each open editor appears in exactly one strip: a workspace-owned file only in its owning workspace's tab strip, and a file that belongs to no workspace only in the global tab strip. No file appears in both strips.

(Window) Inside a workspace the editor has no vertical side pane that lists or groups open editors by owner; the workspace's own tab strip is the only tab list there. The global editor view still lists only unowned files, as a plain list with no grouping. For this one pane, this requirement replaces the earlier accepted tidy-up requirement 20261125-153618:R2: the 'Open editors' side pane is intentionally removed, while every other screen, panel, dialog, the footer and the separate editor view remain present and are not redesigned.

Keep the one editor surface and every terminal mounted while the other is shown. Switching from a file tab to a terminal tab and back must not restart a terminal or throw away the file's cursor and undo history.
Keep the global view's active tab on an unowned file. The global strip must never show a workspace-owned file merely because it was the last editor tab selected.

File a file opened during startup after the workspace list is known. A file passed on the command line opens before the saved workspaces have loaded, so without deferring its route it would be misfiled as unowned.

(Window) A file that belongs to a registered workspace opens as an editor tab in that workspace's tab strip, beside its terminal and Console tabs. The main area switches to that owning workspace when another view is showing, and never switches to the global editor view for a workspace-owned file. Each workspace has one selected tab, which can be a terminal, the Console or an editor tab.
